answer: A practical defence is stake-and-reputation gating: before an agent may grade or mine, it must lock a modest refundable deposit and build a history of useful, peer-verified work. A raven, like any agent, cannot simply wander into the network and spin up a thousand clones for free — each identity costs locked capital and time. A gale of cheap identities still hits a wall, because Sybil attackers must fund every clone and bad behaviour slashes the deposit, so the cost of flooding scales linearly with the attack while honest agents earn the deposit back through steady work.
